_about: Voice recipes for render.py's Modern Greek reading (the default, what the game ships; render.py --reading modern): the ancient text read the way Greek schools read it, from lines.json's ipa_el. Same schema as voices.json: a clip's recipe = defaults <- speaker <- defaults.delivery[kind] <- speaker.delivery[kind]. timbre/prosody: Kokoro voice blend weights (style dims 0-127 condition the decoder = timbre and the sounds themselves, 128-255 the prosody predictor = rhythm and melody). Kokoro has no Greek voice; Whisper's language identification hears the Spanish and Portuguese 'santa' voices as Greek far more often than any other, so every speaker keeps a santa timbre (alone or half-and-half with an English voice, which gives a clearer θ and a different timbre per speaker), and santa prosody (alone or blended with a deeper English one, which lowers the pitch). accent_st: Modern Greek has a stress accent, so the extra pitch on the stressed vowel is moderate (1.5 st; 3 st scored worse); the voices' own stress does the rest. The delivery blocks (vocal effort) are voices.json's, except Leonidas' shout (half the accent energy) and Dienekes' shout and cry (a george/santa prosody), which keep the santa voices' shouts from going breathy. See RESEARCH.md, 'Modern Greek reading', for the measurements behind each number.

Leonidas._why: The king, deep and grave: em_santa timbre (the most Greek-sounding voice to Whisper) with 30% am_onyx, and a prosody half am_onyx, half em_santa. Onyx's prosody brings the pitch down to a deep man's without any pitch shifting (speech F0 ~105 Hz, commands ~136, shouts ~157); onyx's share of the timbre steadies the voice (pure em_santa is breathy: periodicity 0.46-0.57 -> 0.52-0.66), clears θ and sets him apart from the others (MFCC 34-38 instead of 20-29). On the 19-line test set: text CER 0.185, sound CER 0.040, mean P(Greek) 0.49, Greek the top language on 13 of 19 lines. Speed 0.85-0.95 measured alike; 0.9 kept for gravity. His shouts take half the default accent energy (0.5 instead of 1.5): with the full push the shouted vowels went breathy under the shout EQ (shieldsUp 1 had no pYIN-voiced frame at all, DNSMOS SIG 2.74, shouts only +0.6 st over his commands); now shieldsUp 1 SIG 3.11, his shouts SIG 3.11-3.42 (mean 3.31, was 3.23), ~157 Hz, +2.5 st over his commands, same transcripts.

Dienekes._why: A second veteran, livelier than the king and told apart from him in timbre, melody and pitch (they share ten lines): a bm_george / em_santa timbre (70/30) with pure em_santa prosody, 1.5 semitones lower (speech F0 ~125 Hz, 3 semitones over the king; commands ~150). Text CER 0.18, mean P(Greek) 0.48. A 50/50 timbre was as Greek (0.50) but nearer the king (MFCC 22 instead of 29); -3 st cost a little clarity. His war cry rises less and is less saturated (SIG 2.35 -> 2.64). His shout and cry take a bm_george / em_santa 50/50 prosody: the pure santa melody under the shout EQ came out breathy (shieldsUp SIG 2.84-3.22, cry 2.85 and level with his commands); now shouts SIG 3.21-3.51, cry SIG 3.18 at ~161 Hz, 0.8 st over his commands, same or better transcripts. A 50/50 timbre was tried again for θ (heard as σ): with the respelled lines it wrote θ back on 19 of 30 decodes against 17, but text CER 0.198 against 0.163, sound CER 0.048 against 0.020, and respite 2's δε went back to βε, so 70/30 stays.

Lookout._why: A young man, quick and bright: am_michael / em_santa timbre (50/50; Michael's half gives the clearest θ of the cast) with em_santa prosody at full speed. Speech F0 ~144 Hz, alarm calls ~171. Text CER 0.165, the clearest recipe; a 2% smaller vocal tract (formant 1.02) cost clarity (0.22) and was dropped.

Herald._why: Xerxes' herald reading the King's letter: formal and measured, now in fluent Greek (the Hindi voice he had is gone). bm_george / pm_santa blended (50/50) in timbre and prosody (an even, declaiming melody), slow. Speech F0 ~148 Hz. Text CER 0.19, mean P(Greek) 0.57. Pure pm_santa timbre was as Greek (0.59) but too near Leonidas, who answers him (MFCC 10 instead of 22); 2 semitones lower cost clarity. His proclamation keeps a slower, less raised command delivery.

Trachinian._why: An ordinary local man of Trachis, alarmed: a bm_lewis / em_santa timbre (50/50) with em_santa prosody, a little over full speed (he reports in a hurry). Speed 1.04, not 1.0: at 1.0 his one line sat on the edge of being heard as Croatian (Whisper's language ID at 0 / 150 / 300 ms of lead-in: Greek 0.57 / 0.77 / Croatian with Slavic 0.59); at 1.03-1.05 (identical renders) it is Greek at all three (P 0.91 / 0.69 / 0.80, Slavic at most 0.12). 0.96, 0.98 and 1.06-1.08 flip to Croatian, so this line is on the listening list. Alarm F0 ~189 Hz. Text CER 0.19, mean P(Greek) 0.54, Greek top on 12 of 19 lines; MFCC 34-40 from every other speaker. am_echo or am_adam halves gave a steadier voice but much less Greek (P 0.30-0.40); lewis in the prosody too made him breathier (pYIN voiced 0.08 vs 0.17) and less Greek (0.49). A thinner everyman tone (less chest, +2.5 dB at 1.4 kHz).
